q: My husband and I are planning to book the trip fully refundable, but I am worried about something terrible happening health-wise while we are there and it ruining the wedding.
cx: US, 6 weeks, a family destination wedding falls at 18 weeks.

q: I am considering asking my husband to go by himself, although because it is so early we have not yet told his family and we were not planning to until I am 12 weeks.
cx: Same author, travel plans tangled with when to tell family.

q: Of course google is telling me the worst so now I’m spiraling.
cx: 10 weeks, symptoms fading, weeks until the next appointment.

q: My last appointment was at 7w2d and my next is June 2nd at 13w2d. My doctor says I’m perfectly healthy, everything looked fine, we saw the heartbeat and everything. But my next appointment seems so far!!
cx: Same author on the six-week gap between first-trimester visits.

q: I think I may check out a private clinic because I know my OB has nothing coming up & my appointment after that is June 29
cx: Same author considering a paid scan to fill the gap.

q: i did end up getting a doppler which worked after 17 weeks, not before then so i’d be careful when using those.
cx: Same author three months later at 25 weeks, reporting back.

q: The problem is that if I did get it, I wouldn’t qualify for FMLA as I wouldn’t have worked 12 months prior in the position. What I would get is 12 days of leave – based on the company’s policy
cx: US federal employee, 14 weeks with a toddler, weighing a school-district job offer.

q: Under federal service, I’d get a standard 12 weeks. How do I give that up? Except there’s a caveat – accepting 12 weeks of leave in federal service means you agree to work the 12 weeks following your leave or pay it back.
cx: Same author on the leave she would lose by moving.

q: So, apply for new positions and accept a substantially less amount of maternity leave and a “good luck” from a new employer, or keep slowly dying from corporate paralysis for at least another year, but get 3 months with your newborn?
cx: Same author putting the choice to strangers.

q: Last time I signed the agreement I was very pregnant so must have been a little brain foggy!
cx: Same author on misremembering her first leave agreement's terms.

q: He has told me that since I'm on maternity leave, the baby should be my responsibility period, even during times he is not working.
cx: First baby, eight weeks; husband working, she on leave.

q: In the past 8 weeks, he has not once taken over so that I can do something for myself.
cx: Same author.

q: I was so excited to have my nausea subside as it was actually ruining my life.
cx: 12 weeks, nausea easing but she still cannot keep food down.

q: I just hate having to constantly advocate for myself. I know everyone experiences pregnancy differently but this just feels off.
cx: Same author after being told it could be a stomach bug.

q: My M.I.L is here to help us, and she‘s been handling my toddler during the day, and night (she rarely sleeps through). My husband also only got a week off of work, but has been stretched thin doing everything.
cx: One week after a second birth, toddler of 15 months.

q: I feel so much guilt that I have mostly neglected my toddler and that she’s feeling it.
cx: Same author, two under two.

q: I know he’s exhausted but not telling me, same with his mom who has been cooking, cleaning and handling my toddler and sometimes the newborn.
cx: Same author on helpers wearing thin.

q: I’m kinda spiralling now at home as the owner expected me to work 50 hours in 6 days being 12 weeks pregnant. Am I being dramatic?
cx: Runs a florist shop; sent herself home after a sixth straight day.

q: I also don’t really get breaks so yesterday I managed to sit down for 10 minutes in 9 hours.
cx: Same author.

q: I’m struggling to have the conversation with work, I wish I had seen my hours and said something but can I?
cx: Same author, unsure she may raise hours with her boss.

q: As an obese person who has fought for weight loss for years, seeing that number go up - even though I understand that most of it is purely baby-related (I've literally slimmed down in other places) - triggers major self-esteem issues.
cx: Second pregnancy, 25 weeks, weighed at another clinic.

q: I've tried like 4 different brands and the recommended sizes for my weight, so I'm to the point where I want her to tell me what's acceptable.
cx: Same author on compression socks for swelling.
